app.title: River and reservoir pollutant receiving-capacity calculator (API)
app.summary: The person downloads a sample workbook and fills it in. For each water functional zone they give the target concentration, decay coefficient, non-uniformity coefficient, velocity–flow coefficients and reach length, plus the tributaries that join it. They add one daily-flow sheet per scheme and, if needed, reservoir parameters and daily storage. They upload the workbook to the compute endpoint. It splits each main channel at the tributary inflow points, works out each zone's daily receiving capacity and carries the outflow concentration downstream, then averages to months and to a typical year. They get the results back as a multi-sheet Excel file or as JSON. The JSON has a preview of the parsed zones and branches, run counts and the result tables.

task.text: Compute how much pollutant each water functional zone of a river or reservoir can take each year under one or more flow scenarios, from zone parameters and daily flow or storage records.

data.text: A workbook of model parameters for each functional zone, including where its tributaries join, plus daily flow series for each scenario and optional reservoir parameters with daily storage volumes
data.item: a water functional zone (a river reach with its tributaries, or a reservoir) with its parameters and daily flow or storage

stage.text: computing receiving capacity per functional zone from prepared parameters and flow records, before reporting

mechanism.text: A web API, driven through its auto-generated docs page, takes one uploaded workbook and runs the whole calculation in a single request. A format field picks the output: an Excel download, or JSON with a parameter preview, run counts and every result table.

field.text: water environmental capacity calculation for functional zones in water resources engineering

workflow.name: compute a model quantity per unit from a parameter workbook and export result tables

steps.here: download the sample workbook, fill in the vertical zone-input sheet, one daily-flow sheet per scheme and optional reservoir sheets, then upload it to the compute endpoint
JSON output echoes a table of zones with Cs, K, b, a, β, length and C0, a table of branches with length, join position and C0, and the first rows of flow

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: for each day and zone, velocity u = a·Q^β; the main channel is split at tributary join points, inflows are flow-weighted at mixing points, and the capacity formula is summed over main-channel segments, with outflow concentration passed to the next zone

steps.step: summarize to periods and per unit
steps.here: daily capacity is averaged to months, then to a multi-year month-by-zone table with an annual total; process and result tables give average Q, C0, outflow concentration and W per segment

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: if reservoir sheets exist, daily storage is averaged to months by hydrological year (April–March) and W = 31.536·K·V·Cs·b gives monthly capacity per reservoir
the format field returns an xlsx with one sheet per result per scheme, or JSON with the results, counts, elapsed time and the xlsx as base64

distinctive: main channel split into segments at tributary inflow points, with flow-weighted concentration mixing at each junction
a zone with no initial concentration takes the outflow concentration of the zone upstream, chaining zones along the river
several flow scenarios (方案N sheets) computed in one run, each with its own set of result sheets
reservoir capacity uses a storage-volume formula averaged over hydrological years running April to March
parameters come in a fixed vertical sheet layout, one column per zone and five rows per tributary
